rationale: Round 1 failed with a compiler internal error, so this candidate flattens all weights into a moderate, balanced band (0.2-0.6) avoiding the extremes likely responsible for the internal failure, while keeping all seven passes enabled. The program is a small (195 lines, 12 functions, ~1.3 KB text) bit-serial decoder from BitBench whose hot path is the five11/read_11_bits bit-pumping loop, so SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since instruction substitution is cheap, safe, and effective against pattern-matching of its small arithmetic kernels, while BCF and FLA are kept at moderate security weights with elevated RuntimeCost (0.5-0.6) so the selector applies them selectively rather than blanket-applying opaque predicates and flattening to the hot loop. SPLIT and IGV carry low runtime/size costs and decent diversity gain to add structural variety across the 12 functions cheaply, and IBR/ICALL sit at mid-band values to contribute block-level indirection without dominating selection. CorrectnessRisk is uniformly kept low-to-moderate (0.1-0.3) to preserve correctness on this control-flow-dense benchmark.
